newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW - Sweden Riksbank repo cut, inflation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Sweden Riksbank repo cut, inflation.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' reactions to the Swedish Riksbank's 10-basis point cut in its key repo rate to 5.05 percent and its September inflation report on Tuesday.
The central bank said in the report there were good prospects of meeting its two-percent inflation target in 1997 and the first half of 1998 and that there was scope for more repo rate cuts.
ANDERS BORSCHENIUS, ANALYST AT DEN DANSKE BANK IN COPENHAGEN
"The repo cut was in line with what we had expected. We may consider lowering our forecast for where the rate will bottom out to 4.50 percent from 4.75 percent."

Borschenius told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) the Riksbank's economic growth forecast of three to four percent for 1997 and 1998 combined was within reach but warned of the inflationary effects of wage increases.
"We need to see a better framework for negatiating wages. That's the real threat to inflation at the moment.
"This (report) was a little more positive than the June report. The crown is now valued in line with the balances in the economy, but there's a risk to exports from the crown appreciation."
JAN HAGGSTROM, ECONOMIST AT HANDELSBANKEN IN STOCKHOLM

"Some elements of the report were more optimistic than we had expected. The bank can see growth without inflation. I see the repo rate at 4.50 percent in December, but I wouldn't rule out further cuts beyond that point.
"Clearly, wage increases have been much too high, but we must remember that when the wage deals were struck, inflationary expectations were much higher.

"Economic fundamentals are looking quite good, but uncertainty surrounding the EMU may stop bond yields falling further. The market is too pessimistic at the short end of the yield curve," Haggstrom told RFTV.
